text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Foreign Minister Sheikh Sabah al-Ahmad al-Sabah says U.S. troops in Kuwait to stay as long as Iraqi President Saddam Hussein remains in power.
- Five parliamentarians propose a bill to ban concerts and fashion shows.
- Foreign Minister says Kuwait will not resume relations with Iraq as long as the Iraqi regime remains in power.
- Constitutional Court rejects case by former deputy Ali al-Baghli who challenges the results of the October parliamentary election.
- Drinking water in Kuwait not polluted, says Electricity and Water Ministry official.
- Parliamentary panel, health minister review plan to improve state health services.
- Sudan seeks reconciliation with Kuwait. Ties between the two states were strained over what Kuwait describes as Sudan's sympathy with Iraq during its 1990-91 occupation of Kuwait.
